title: Getting started with `cityClimateHealth`
text: built-arguments argvar arglag can override ’d like, defaults : maxlag: default 5 (days) argvar: default ns() knots 50th 90th percentile unit-specific exposure. arglag: default list(fun = 'ns', knots = logknots(maxlag, nk = 2)) can also affect global centering point: default behavior global_cen = NULL, meaning mininum RR used can override setting global_cen

previous_headings: Run the model > Run the conditional poisson model
title: Getting started with `cityClimateHealth`
text: Now several options running conditional poisson model: show code just run condPois_2stage vignette. condPois_1stage call look like , ’d need add argument multi_zone = T multiple geo_units ma_exposure_matrix: See one-stage demo details. Note forest_plot spatial_plot implemented condPois_1stage since can get information RR plot. condPois_sb, additional information ’d need shapefile showing geo_units arranged, case ma_towns (test run code took 20 minutes complete full MA dataset [maybe additional bugs work ]): See Bayesian demo details.
code: ma_model <- condPois_2stage(ma_exposure_matrix,                              ma_outcomes_tbl,                             verbose = 1,                             global_cen = 15) #> -- validation passed #> -- stage 1 #>  #> crossbasis args for geo_unit  ACTON : #>  #> maxlag: 5  #>  #> argvar: #> List of 2 #>  $ fun  : chr "ns" #>  $ knots: Named num [1:2] 25.6 31.4 #>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "50%" "90%" #>  #> arglag: #> List of 2 #>  $ fun  : chr "ns" #>  $ knots: num [1:2] 0.878 2.095 #>  #> strata: #> ACTON:yr2012:mn05:dow03 #> strata_min: 0  #>  #> min_n: 50  #>  #> truncate final RR and basis cen:  0  #> formula: #>    daily_deaths ~ cb #> family: quasipoisson #>  #> -- mixmeta #> formula: coef_matrix ~ exp_mean + exp_IQR #> random: ~ 1 | COUNTY20/TOWN20  #> -- stage 2 #> truncate final RR and basis cen:  0.01 ma_model <- condPois_1stage(ma_exposure_matrix, ma_outcomes_tbl,                              multi_zone = T,                             global_cen = 15) data("ma_towns") ma_model <- condPois_sb(ma_exposure_matrix, ma_outcomes_tbl,                          global_cen = 15, ma_towns)

title: One set of Heat-Health Associations for a single or multiple zones using `cityClimateHealth`
text: Now, ’ll walk basic DLNM heat-health associations single zone. assumes basic knowledge library(dlnm). libraries ’ll need run conditional poisson model. inputs define crossbasis matrix. use default ns behavior tails distribution linear. put lists argvar arglag: Limit columns exposure matrix just ones maxlag: Now run model Notice dispersion parameter quite high! , simulated data – part quasipoisson model works used re-scale variance covariance matrix. Next get crosspred outputs correctly centered minimum RR plot  Finally, basic checks math using utility functions estimate dispersion parameters variance-covariance matrix. functions useful longer using R functions estimate model. First check dispersion Next check vcov
code: library(dlnm) library(gnm) library(ggplot2) library(data.table) arg_fun = 'ns' lag_fun = 'ns' x_knots = quantile(boston_exposure_mat$tmax_C, probs = c(0.5, 0.9)) maxlag = 5 nk = 2 argvar <- list(fun = arg_fun, knots = x_knots) arglag <- list(fun = lag_fun, knots = logknots(maxlag, nk = nk)) xcols <- c('tmax_C', paste0('explag',1:maxlag)) x_mat <- boston_exposure_mat[, ..xcols]  cb <- crossbasis(x_mat, lag = maxlag, argvar = argvar, arglag = arglag) m_sub <- gnm(daily_deaths ~ cb,              data = boston_deaths_tbl,              family = quasipoisson,              eliminate = factor(strata),              subset = strata_total > 0) summary(m_sub) #>  #> Call: #> gnm(formula = daily_deaths ~ cb, eliminate = factor(strata),  #>     family = quasipoisson, data = boston_deaths_tbl, subset = strata_total >  #>         0) #>  #> Deviance Residuals:  #>      Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max   #> -4.01375  -1.24434   0.02461   1.28224   4.31338   #>  #> Coefficients of interest: #>           Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> cbv1.l1  0.0109784  0.0164413   0.668  0.50453     #> cbv1.l2  0.0006729  0.0149994   0.045  0.96423     #> cbv1.l3  0.1163359  0.0090989  12.786  < 2e-16 *** #> cbv1.l4 -0.0534439  0.0090748  -5.889 6.04e-09 *** #> cbv2.l1  0.0672159  0.0527738   1.274  0.20321     #> cbv2.l2  0.0180828  0.0491205   0.368  0.71289     #> cbv2.l3  0.2108521  0.0327248   6.443 2.18e-10 *** #> cbv2.l4 -0.0986866  0.0330841  -2.983  0.00296 **  #> cbv3.l1  0.0862389  0.0356515   2.419  0.01582 *   #> cbv3.l2 -0.0170908  0.0314134  -0.544  0.58657     #> cbv3.l3  0.1735069  0.0211209   8.215  < 2e-16 *** #> cbv3.l4 -0.0855985  0.0202383  -4.230 2.65e-05 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> (Dispersion parameter for quasipoisson family taken to be 3.753814) #>  #> Residual deviance: 2614.7 on 696 degrees of freedom #> AIC: NA #>  #> Number of iterations: 2 cp <- crosspred(cb, m_sub, cen = 20, by = 0.1)  cen = cp$predvar[which.min(cp$allRRfit)]  cp <- crosspred(cb, m_sub, cen = cen, by = 0.1) plot_cp = data.frame(     x = cp$predvar,     RR = cp$allRRfit,     RRlb = cp$allRRlow,     RRhigh = cp$allRRhigh )  ggplot(plot_cp, aes(x = x, y = RR, ymin = RRlb, ymax = RRhigh)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = '11') +   theme_classic() +   geom_ribbon(fill = 'grey75', alpha = 0.2) +   geom_line() + xlab("Tmax (degC)") dispersion <- calc_dispersion(y = boston_deaths_tbl$daily_deaths,                  X = cb,                  stratum_vector = boston_deaths_tbl$strata,                  beta = coef(m_sub)) dispersion #> [1] 3.753814 vcov_beta <- calc_vcov(y = boston_deaths_tbl$daily_deaths,                  X = cb,                  stratum_vector = boston_deaths_tbl$strata,                  beta = coef(m_sub))  # update with the dipserion parameter t1 <- vcov_beta * dispersion  # check against the original model's vcov t2 <- vcov(m_sub) attributes(t2) <- NULL t2 <- matrix(t2, nrow = nrow(t1), ncol = ncol(t1))  # should be the same all.equal(t1, t2, tolerance = 1e-8) #> [1] TRUE

title: one_stage_time_series_demo
text: Now, ’ll walk basic DLNM heat-health associations single zone. assumes basic knowledge library(dlnm). libraries ’ll need run time-series model. inputs define crossbasis matrix. use default ns behavior tails distribution linear. put lists argvar arglag: Time-series models depend adjustment short- long-term time-trends, seasonality. , using summer months rather whole year data, use default 4 degrees freedom natural splines. Limit columns exposure matrix just ones maxlag: Now run model: Notice dispersion parameter quite high! , simulated data – part quasipoisson model works used re-scale variance covariance matrix. Next get crosspred outputs correctly centered minimum RR plot:
code: library(dlnm) library(ggplot2) library(data.table) arg_fun = 'ns' lag_fun = 'ns' x_knots = quantile(boston_exposure_mat$tmax_C, probs = c(0.5, 0.9)) maxlag = 5 nk = 2 argvar <- list(fun = arg_fun, knots = x_knots) arglag <- list(fun = lag_fun, knots = logknots(maxlag, nk = nk)) library(splines)  boston_deaths_tbl$time_index <- as.numeric(boston_deaths_tbl$date - min(boston_deaths_tbl$date))  time_trend <- ns(boston_deaths_tbl$time_index, df = 4) xcols <- c('tmax_C', paste0('explag',1:maxlag)) x_mat <- boston_exposure_mat[, ..xcols]  cb <- crossbasis(x_mat, lag = maxlag, argvar = argvar, arglag = arglag) m_sub <- glm(daily_deaths ~ cb + dow + time_trend,              data = boston_deaths_tbl,              family = quasipoisson) summary(m_sub) #>  #> Call: #> glm(formula = daily_deaths ~ cb + dow + time_trend, family = quasipoisson,  #>     data = boston_deaths_tbl) #>  #> Coefficients: #>               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> (Intercept)  7.6093176  0.0169805 448.120  < 2e-16 *** #> cbv1.l1      0.0085430  0.0144278   0.592 0.553919     #> cbv1.l2     -0.0013017  0.0130616  -0.100 0.920635     #> cbv1.l3      0.1076614  0.0075067  14.342  < 2e-16 *** #> cbv1.l4     -0.0571907  0.0081346  -7.031 4.07e-12 *** #> cbv2.l1      0.0464620  0.0476158   0.976 0.329441     #> cbv2.l2      0.0415549  0.0436321   0.952 0.341153     #> cbv2.l3      0.1737757  0.0295840   5.874 5.98e-09 *** #> cbv2.l4     -0.1108638  0.0295266  -3.755 0.000185 *** #> cbv3.l1      0.0728392  0.0325889   2.235 0.025656 *   #> cbv3.l2      0.0022551  0.0285686   0.079 0.937100     #> cbv3.l3      0.1538317  0.0188800   8.148 1.23e-15 *** #> cbv3.l4     -0.0934208  0.0186368  -5.013 6.46e-07 *** #> dow          0.0004160  0.0006459   0.644 0.519724     #> time_trend1  0.1122725  0.0064961  17.283  < 2e-16 *** #> time_trend2  0.1621481  0.0060714  26.707  < 2e-16 *** #> time_trend3  0.2586710  0.0111667  23.165  < 2e-16 *** #> time_trend4  0.2107506  0.0050532  41.706  < 2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> (Dispersion parameter for quasipoisson family taken to be 3.851407) #>  #>     Null deviance: 21566.0  on 917  degrees of freedom #> Residual deviance:  3466.8  on 900  degrees of freedom #> AIC: NA #>  #> Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 3 cp <- crosspred(cb, m_sub, cen = 20, by = 0.1)  cen = cp$predvar[which.min(cp$allRRfit)]  cp <- crosspred(cb, m_sub, cen = cen, by = 0.1) plot_cp = data.frame(     x = cp$predvar,     RR = cp$allRRfit,     RRlb = cp$allRRlow,     RRhigh = cp$allRRhigh )  ggplot(plot_cp, aes(x = x, y = RR, ymin = RRlb, ymax = RRhigh)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = '11') +   theme_classic() +   geom_ribbon(fill = 'grey75', alpha = 0.2) +   geom_line() + xlab("Tmax (degC)")

title: Add a population column to an outcome table, for use as a population offset in timeseries_1stage_glm() — add_population_offset
text: outcomes_tbl object class "outcome", produced make_outcome_table() population_data data.frame/data.table population estimates. Commonly one row per geo_unit per year (e.g. annual census/ACS estimates), can also one row per geo_unit per day finer-grained estimates. population_columns named list mapping columns population_data. Must include: "geo_unit": column identifying geographic unit (must use codes/values outcomes_tbl's geo_unit column) "population": column population value (numeric, > 0) EITHER "year" (integer year, annual population data – typical case) "date" (daily/finer population data) – supply exactly one , population_col_name name new column add outcomes_tbl. Default "population". string pass population_col timeseries_1stage_glm(). verbose print short confirmation message. Default TRUE.

"annual" (default) fits single smooth spline calendar date (ns(time_num, df = df_time)) appropriate continuous, full-year daily data.
